diagnostic_evidence.quote: We know that $\alpha$ is homogeneous, that is, $h_z\circ \alpha = \alpha\circ T^*h_z$. Moreover, given a bisection $L$, the inverse restricted to $L$, $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ is also homogeneous: $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}\circ h_z = T^*h_z\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims that for ANY Lagrangian bisection $L$ of a local symplectic groupoid integrating a homogeneous Poisson manifold, the induced diffeomorphism $\phi_L = \beta\circ\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ is a HOMOGENEOUS Poisson diffeomorphism. The supporting remark claims that for any bisection $L$ the restricted inverse $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ is equivariant, $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}\circ h_z = T^*h_z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$, because $\alpha$ is homogeneous. This inference is invalid: the right-hand side $T^*h_z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{|L}(x)$ is the image of the source-fiber point over $x$ under the phase lift, which lies in $\Sigma$ but need not lie in $L$; equality with $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}(h_z x)$ holds exactly when $L$ is $\mathbb R^\times$-invariant (i.e., $T^*h_z(L)=L$). No such invariance is assumed in the proposition. Hence item (1) (homogeneity of $\phi_L$) is unestablished, and is false for general (non-invariant) Lagrangian bisections, e.g. bisections given as images of closed 1-forms $\mu$ that are not 1-homogeneous (cf. Proposition prop: mu closed, which shows invariance of the image is equivalent to 1-homogeneity of the form).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that the bisection $L$ is homogeneous ($\mathbb R^\times$-invariant); then the remark's computation $\alpha^{-1}_{|L}\circ h_z = T^*h_z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ is valid and the proposition holds as stated. This is a standard local hypothesis, already satisfied by all bisection families used in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: Item (1) of Proposition prop:added-4, and the prose claims built on it (e.g. that any Lagrangian bisection of the constructed bi-realization induces a homogeneous Poisson diffeomorphism), are unsupported as stated; only the Poisson part is established by the cited source. The Jacobi-integrator construction itself is unaffected because it uses exact families of homogeneous Lagrangian bisections.
issues.title: Homogeneity of induced diffeomorphism asserted for arbitrary Lagrangian bisections without invariance hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis that $L$ be $\mathbb R^\times$-invariant (one word in the statement) makes the remark's computation valid; the construction of the integrators only ever uses homogeneous Lagrangian bisections, so no substantive claim, rate, or advertised scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given an exact smooth family of Lagrangian bisections such that $L_0$ is the zero section, constructing a suitable approximation of the variation functions $(\mathcal{H}_s)_s$ that coincides with $ H^P$ of order $k$, the induced family of diffeomorphisms $(\varphi_{L_s})_{s\in I}$ is a homogeneous Hamiltonian Poisson integrator of order $k$ for $H^P$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Conclusion asserts that the method 'preserves not only the Jacobi structure and the Hamiltonian'. What the paper establishes is: (i) the step maps are Jacobi (resp. homogeneous Poisson) diffeomorphisms, so the structure is preserved exactly; (ii) the maps are time-epsilon flows of modified Hamiltonians $(\mathcal H_s)$ with $\mathcal H_s = H^J + o(s^{k-1})$ (per the definitions of JHI/hPHI), i.e. the Hamiltonian is preserved only up to the order $k$ of the method, exactly as the Introduction states for PHI ('preserving the Poisson structure and the Hamiltonian (up to a certain order)'). Exact preservation of $H$ is never established; the Hamiltonian is only an invariant of the modified (order-dependent) Hamiltonian system, so it is conserved along the numerical flow only to the advertised order.

failure_location.quote: This approach preserves not only the Jacobi structure and the Hamiltonian, but also the induced foliation and Casimir functions, which is particularly relevant in mechanical applications.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the sentence to 'preserves the Jacobi structure exactly and the Hamiltonian up to the order of the method' (matching the qualification already used for PHI in the Introduction); no other content is affected.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding summary overstates the guarantee for the Hamiltonian: readers are told the scheme preserves $H$, whereas the framework only delivers preservation up to the order of the method (exact preservation of the modified Hamiltonian).
issues.title: Conclusion claims the method preserves the Hamiltonian, but only order-k preservation is established
issues.why_classification: A local qualifier restores accuracy; the method, its order, and its advertised structure-preservation guarantees all survive unchanged, so the repair is short and loses nothing.
